nodes.name: Lead posted by another system
nodes.notes:
Stands in for an ad platform, Typeform, or anything else that can post JSON.

The shared secret is checked by n8n against a credential, not by a node in this workflow: a key written into the workflow would end up in the exported JSON and then in git.

nodes.name: Read the lead
nodes.notes: Maps this platform's field names onto the standard lead. A new source means a new copy of THIS node, and nothing else changes.

nodes.name: Hand it to the pipeline
nodes.notes: Does NOT wait for the pipeline to finish. The sender gets its 202 immediately; scoring and the CRM happen behind it. An ad platform that waits three seconds for a reply starts retrying.

nodes.name: Reply: accepted

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ accepted: true, lead_id: $('Read the lead').item.json.lead.lead_id || null, message: 'Lead accepted for processing.' }) }}

nodes.notes: 202 Accepted, not 200 OK: the lead has been taken, but the work is not finished yet. Ad platforms treat both as success and stop retrying.

assignments.name: error
assignments.value: The posted payload had no email, phone or message - nothing to contact or judge.

nodes.name: Send to quarantine
nodes.notes: Even a rejected payload is kept. A silently discarded lead is the failure this whole project exists to prevent.

nodes.name: Reply: not a usable lead

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ accepted: false, message: 'No email, phone or message in the payload. It has been recorded for review.' }) }}

nodes.notes: 400 tells whoever is sending that their integration is wrong. A 200 here would let a broken form post nothing for weeks unnoticed.
